newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan rubber seen bearish, bottom limited.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan rubber seen bearish, bottom limited.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to remain bearish this week on the view that ample domestic rubber stocks have not reached their ceiling, but sharp falls could be avoided due to feelings the market has been oversold, traders said on Monday.
"Market sentiment remains bearish. Until Japan's rubber stocks hit a peak, private investors are unlikely to place fresh buying," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Traders said rubber stocks were expected to continue rising at least until the end of this month.
The benchmark March contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 131.1 yen per kg, against 132.5 yen last Friday.
Similarly on the Kobe Rubber Exchange, the key March contract was quoted at 131.5 yen in the second morning session, down from 132.0 yen last Friday.

Traders said market participants were expecting a large number of deliveries when the spot contract expires later this month, given continued growth in rubber stocks, but added there will not be many who would be willing to take deliveries.
Because of such expectations, there is the possibility of the spot October contract expiring sharply lower than its current level, and this has cast a shadow on Japan's rubber markets.

Some traders also said the dissolution of the Thai parliament and the government's decision to call elections in November spurred concern here that the government may temporarily stop its rubber price support system.
"Uncertainty over the Thai government's price support system, reflecting the political turmoil in that country, is also a psychologically bearish factor for Japan's markets," one trader said.
On the other hand, there was also a hint of caution due to the feeling the market was oversold after most Japanese rubber futures hit their life-of-contract lows last week.
"Domestic rubber futures were much lower than the level of Thai rubber offer prices to Japan, and this could fuel a short-covering rally," another trader said.
He added that support of 130 yen per kg for the benchmark March contract was likely to be maintained.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were quoted at 122 U.S. cents on a free-on-board (FOB) basis as of Monday, down one cent from last Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber to large-lot end users was quoted at 144 yen per kg as of Monday, against 143 yen on October 1. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk (813-3432-7431)
